title: Amalickiah Leads the Angry Gathering

explicit_facts.text: Those who would not heed Helaman and his brethren gathered against their brethren.
The gathered people were exceedingly angry and determined to kill their brethren.
Amalickiah was a large, strong man who led those who were angry against their brethren.

unspecified_visual_details: The gathering place, clothing, weapons, and number of people are not specified.
Helaman and his brethren are mentioned, but their physical presence at the gathering is not established.

narration.text: And it came to pass that as many as would not hearken to the words of Helaman and his brethren were gathered together against their brethren.
they were exceedingly wroth, insomuch that they were determined to slay them.
Now the leader of those who were wroth against their brethren was a large and a strong man; and his name was Amalickiah.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an attack or killing; the verses state intent, not an act.
Do not assume Helaman and his brethren are physically present at the gathering.

title: Amalickiah's ambition

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent direct dialogue for Amalickiah or the people.

title: The people divide
summary: Many church members believed Amalickiah's flattering words and dissented. The narrator reflects on how quickly people forget the Lord and how much wickedness one wicked man can cause.

explicit_facts.text: Many in the church believed Amalickiah's flattering words and dissented; the affairs of the Nephites became precarious despite a recent victory and rejoicing over deliverance from the Lamanites.

The narrator says one wicked man can cause great wickedness among people.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord or the evil one as visible figures; they are mentioned in the narrator's reflection.

title: Moroni hears of dissension
summary: Amalickiah led many people toward wickedness and toward seeking to destroy the church of God and the foundation of liberty. Moroni heard of the dissensions and was angry with Amalickiah.

explicit_facts.text: Amalickiah used cunning and flattering words to lead many people toward wickedness and toward seeking to destroy the church of God and the foundation of liberty.

unspecified_visual_details: Moroni's location and how he heard of the dissensions are not stated.

title: The title of liberty

explicit_facts.text: Moroni tore his coat, wrote on a piece of it, and fastened it to the end of a pole.

The writing on the cloth was “In memory of our God, our religion, and freedom, and our peace, our wives, and our children”.
